chunks: And ʿAbdullāh ibn Miskān narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, who said:

Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, distinguished His Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله with noble character traits. So examine yourselves; if they are found in you, then praise Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and desire from Him an increase in them. Then he mentioned them as ten: certainty, contentment, patience, gratitude, forbearance, good character, generosity, protective jealousy, courage, and manliness.

key_terms.الْقَنَاعَةَ: contentment with what one has been given
key_terms.مَكَارِمِ الْأَخْلَاقِ: the highest and most noble moral qualities

ai.seo_question: What noble character traits did Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام say believers should examine in themselves?
ai.summary: This hadith states that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, specially granted His Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله noble moral virtues. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام instructs believers to examine themselves for these qualities, to praise Allah if they possess them, and to ask Him for increase in them. The hadith then lists ten foundational virtues of excellent character.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.4901 - Abdullah ibn Muskan narrated from Abu Abdullah Al-Sadiq (as) who said:
"Indeed, Allah (swt), the Blessed and Exalted, distinguished His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) with noble character traits.
Therefore, examine yourselves, and if you find these traits within you, then praise Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, and seek from Him (swt) an increase in them."
He (as) then mentioned ten traits: certainty (yaqin), contentment (qana'ah), patience (sabr), gratitude (shukr), forbearance (hilm), good manners (husn al-khuluq), generosity (sakha'), protective jealousy (ghayrah), courage (shuja'ah), and honor (muru'ah).
